evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need (creating a game with basic details) without prescribing specific UI widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: States a functional need (inviting via URL) without dictating technical implementation details beyond the concept of a URL.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget/format (single multi-line text field) rather than just the need to enter an item to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need (viewing all items) without specifying UI or implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the capability needed (selecting an item) without prescribing how selection is implemented in UI/tech.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to add items; does not mandate specific UI controls or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Captures the stakeholder need (editing items) without solution-level prescriptions.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States desired functionality without specifying UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a behavioral need (reveal estimates early) without prescribing how it is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Defines a business rule/need (use average) rather than a concrete technical mechanism or UI detail.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element/behavior (“estimate” field auto-filled) instead of stating the underlying need (speeding acceptance when unanimous).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the need to record an agreed estimate without specifying UI widgets or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes the capability (re-estimation) without prescribing solution details.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific source/format (“spreadsheet”) as the mechanism rather than stating the broader need to bulk-load stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete interaction/solution approach (copy/paste from spreadsheet) instead of the underlying need to quickly add multiple stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: States the user need (finding previous games) without mandating UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need without prescribing export formats or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete storage/export format (HTML file) rather than the need to save/share a transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export/storage format (CSV) instead of the stakeholder need to further process transcript data.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need (remove a game and its data) without specifying technical deletion mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required information to fulfill the need (account creation) but does not prescribe concrete UI widgets or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: States authentication need without prescribing UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to update account information without solution-level prescriptions.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States desired outcome (account and associated data removed) without implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need (localized time display) without prescribing technical approach.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism/channel (by email) rather than the underlying need to recover access after forgetting a password.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Overly prescribes concrete solution choices (exact card sets/sequences) instead of the need to support different estimation scales.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Imposes a specific numeric limit (15) that is a solution constraint rather than expressing the underlying need (support sufficiently large teams).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Primarily states the need to join/identify oneself; mentioning entering a name is input data, not a concrete widget/implementation prescription.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States an information need without prescribing UI or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to view the backlog for the session without solution prescriptions.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes a visibility/feedback need without specifying UI widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: States desired behavior (simultaneous reveal after all votes) without prescribing technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Defines a rule about when changes are allowed; does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need without specifying how it is displayed or stored.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the need for transparency during discussion without solution-level prescriptions.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism and parameter (a two-minute countdown timer) rather than the underlying need to timebox discussion.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Builds on a specific solution construct (two-minute timer) and prescribes automatic reset behavior, i.e., implementation/interaction detail.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to review prior information; “scroll back” is a mild UI hint but not a concrete widget/technical mechanism mandate.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency need for comparison without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Defines allowed behavior; does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI presentation details (small thumbnail photo, displayed near cards) rather than the underlying need for personalization/identity cues.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards/implementation choices (XHTML/CSS compliance) rather than the stakeholder need (broad accessibility/compatibility).

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a documentation/communication need without prescribing a specific technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Directly prescribes a technical implementation detail (database indexes) instead of the need (fast queries/performance).

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Overly prescribes specific technical targets (exact browser versions) rather than the broader need for cross-browser compatibility.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific standard (W3C accessibility guidelines) as the solution approach rather than stating the accessibility need in problem terms.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a performance need without prescribing technical mechanisms to achieve it.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical mechanism/standard (Unicode) rather than the underlying need (support multiple languages/character sets).

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user-facing need (predictable URLs) without prescribing implementation details (routing scheme, formats).

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: States a user experience need without prescribing specific UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a privacy/anonymization need; does not prescribe specific storage formats, algorithms, or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need (usage metrics) without prescribing how metrics are collected or displayed.
